answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expensive to fake: each agent must build a verifiable history of useful work attested by independent peers before it can transact at scale. Like a vine that only grows where it is tended, trust should spread slowly through real interactions, not instant self-declared claims. A newcomer starts at the edge, earns small tasks, and only after a long voyage of consistent, checkable contributions does it reach the oasis of high-value work, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs far more than it can earn.
